{{Short description|none}}
{{wiktionary|Appendix:Glossary of set theory}}
This is a glossary of terms and definitions related to the topic of [[set theory]].

{{Compact ToC|short1|sym=yes|pre1=Greek|x=[[#XYZ|XYZ]]|y=|z=|seealso=yes|refs=yes}}

==Greek==
{{glossary}}

{{term|α|{{mvar|α}}}}
{{defn|defn=Often used for an {{gli|ordinal}}.}}

{{term|β|{{mvar|β}}}}
{{defn|no=1|defn={{mvar|β}}{{mvar|X}} is the [[Stone–Čech compactification]] of {{mvar|X}}.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An ordinal.}}

{{term|γ|{{mvar|γ}}}}
{{defn|defn=A [[Additively indecomposable ordinal|gamma number]], an [[Ordinal number|ordinal]] of the form {{mvar|ω<sup>α</sup>}}.}}

{{term|Γ|{{math|Γ}}}}
{{defn|defn=The [[Veblen function|Gamma function of ordinals]]. In particular {{math|Γ<sub>0</sub>}} is the [[Feferman–Schütte ordinal]].}}

{{term|δ|{{mvar|δ}}}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[delta number]] is an ordinal of the form {{mvar|ω<sup>ω<sup>α</sup></sup>}}.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A limit ordinal.}}

{{term|Δ|content ={{math|Δ}} (Greek capital delta, not to be confused with a triangle ∆)}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A set of formulas in the [[Lévy hierarchy]].}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[delta system]]
}}

{{term|ε|{{mvar|ε}}}}
{{defn|defn=An [[epsilon numbers (mathematics)|epsilon number]], an ordinal with {{math|1=ω<sup>ε</sup>=ε}}.}}

{{term|η|{{mvar|η}}}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The [[order type]] of the [[rational number]]s.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An [[eta set]], a type of ordered set.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn={{mvar|η<sub>α</sub>}} is an [[Erdős cardinal]].}}

{{term|θ|{{mvar|θ}}}}
{{defn|defn=The [[order type]] of the [[real number]]s.}}

{{term|Θ|{{math|Θ}}}}
{{defn|defn=The supremum of the ordinals that are the image of a function from {{mvar|<sup>ω</sup>ω}} (usually in models where the axiom of choice is not assumed).}}

{{term|κ|{{mvar|κ}}}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=Often used for a [[Cardinal number|cardinal]], especially the critical point of an elementary embedding.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Erdős cardinal]] {{math|''κ''(''α'')}} is the smallest cardinal such that {{math|''κ''(''α'') → (''α'')<sup>< ''ω''</sup>}}.}}

{{term|λ|{{mvar|λ}}}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=Often used for a {{gli|cardinal}}.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The order type of the [[real number]]s.}}

{{term|μ|{{mvar|μ}}}}
{{defn|defn=A [[Measure (mathematics)|measure]].}}

{{term|Π|{{math|Π}}}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A product of cardinals.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A set of formulas in the [[Lévy hierarchy]].}}

{{term|ρ|{{mvar|ρ}}}}
{{defn|defn=The [[rank of a set]].}}

{{term|σ|{{mvar|σ}}}}
{{defn|defn=countable, as in [[σ-compact]], σ-complete and so on.}}

{{term|Σ|{{math|Σ}}}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A sum of cardinals.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A set of formulas in the [[Lévy hierarchy]].}}

{{term|φ|{{mvar|φ}}}}
{{defn|defn=A [[Veblen function]].}}

{{term|ω|{{mvar|ω}}}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The smallest infinite ordinal.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn={{mvar|ω<sub>α</sub>}} is an alternative name for {{math|ℵ<sub>''α''</sub>}}, used when it is considered as an ordinal number rather than a cardinal number.}}

{{term|Ω|{{math|Ω}}}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The class of all ordinals, related to [[Cantor's absolute]].}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Ω-logic]] is a form of logic introduced by Hugh Woodin.}}

{{glossary end}}

==!$@==
{{glossary}}

{{term|1=∈, =, ⊆, ⊇, ⊃, ⊂, ∪, ∩, ∅|2={{nobold|1=∈, =, ⊆, ⊇, ⊃, ⊂, ∪, ∩, ∅}}}}
{{defn|defn=Standard first-order set theoretical symbols with their usual definitions, ([[Element (mathematics)|is a member of]], equals, [[Subset|is a subset of]], [[Superset|is a superset of]], [[Superset|is a proper superset of]], [[Subset|is a proper subset of]], union, intersection, empty set)}}

{{term|∧ ∨ → ↔ ¬ ∀ ∃|{{nobold|∧ ∨ → ↔ ¬ ∀ ∃}}}}
{{defn|defn=Standard [[List of logic symbols|logical symbols]] with their usual definitions; and (conjunction), or (inclusive disjunction), implies (conditional), is equivalent to (biconditional), not (negation), for all (universal quantifier), there exists (existential quantifier).}}

{{term|≡|{{math|≡}}}}
{{defn|defn=An equivalence, or congruence relation.}}

{{term|↾}}
{{defn|no 1|defn={{math|f↾X}} once denoted the corestriction of a relation, or mapping, but in modern mathematics is the restriction of a relation, or mapping f, to some set X, as-in,}}
{{defn|no 2|defn= 1.) {{math|f↾X≔{(x,y):x∈X and y∈X}}} — the restriction, and corestriction — for a relation {{math|f}} to {{math|X}}.}}
{{defn|no 3|defn= 2.) {{math|f↾X≔{f(x):x∈X}}} — the restriction of the domain — for a mapping {{math|f}} to {{math|X}}.}}

{{term|↿}}
{{defn|defn={{math|f↿X}} is the restriction of a relation or mapping {{math|f}}, to some set {{math|X}}.}}

{{term|△|content=△ (A triangle, not to be confused with the Greek letter {{math|Δ|size=100%}})}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=For {{math|X△Y}}, the symmetric difference of sets X, and Y, as-in, {{math|X△Y≔{x:x∈X-Y or x∈Y-X}}}.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[diagonal intersection]].}}

{{term|◊}}
{{defn|defn=The [[diamond principle]].}}

{{term|♣}}
{{defn|defn=A [[clubsuit]] principle.}}

{{term|□}}
{{defn|defn=The [[square principle]], or Q.E.D. — quod erat demonstrandum — that which was to be demonstrated.}}

{{term|∘}}
{{defn|defn=The [[Function composition|composition of functions]]}}

{{term|⁀}}
{{defn|no=1|defn={{math|α⁀b}} is the extension of a sequence {{math|a}}, by an element {{math|b}}, as-in,}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=For an α-sequence, {{math|a}}, {{math|a⁀b≔a⨿{b}}} such that b is the α-th element of {{math|a}}.}}

{{term|+}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Ordinal arithmetic#Addition|Addition of ordinals]].}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Cardinal number#Cardinal addition|Addition of cardinals]].}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=α<sup>+</sup> is the successor cardinal, or the least cardinal greater than α.}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=B<sup>+</sup> is the poset of nonzero elements of a Boolean algebra B.}}
{{defn|no=5|defn=The inclusive or operation in a Boolean algebra (in ring theory it is used for the exclusive or operation).}}

{{term|~}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=For sets {{math|a}}, and {{math|b}}, {{math|a~b}} is the set of elements of {{math|a}} not in {{math|b}}, called the difference of, {{math|a}} and {{math|b}}, as-in,}}
{{defn|no=2|defn={{math|a~b≔{α:α∈a and α∉b}}}.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=An equivalence relation.}}

{{term|&setminus;}}
{{defn|defn=Synonym of ~.}}

{{term|−}}
{{defn|defn=Synonym of ~.}}

{{term|≈}}
{{defn|defn=Has the [[Equinumerosity|same cardinality]] as.}}

{{term|×}}
{{defn|defn=For sets {{math|a}}, and {{math|b}}, {{math|a×b≔{(c,d):c∈a and d∈b}}}, called the  [[product of sets]] {{math|a}}, and {{math|b}}.}}

{{term|/}}
{{defn|defn=For a set {{math|a}}, and an equivalence relation {{math|~}}, {{math|a/~≔{b/~:b∈a}}}, called the quotient of a set by an [[equivalence relation]] ~.}}

{{term|×}}
{{defn|defn=For ordinals {{math|a}}, and {{math|b}}, {{math|a×b≔𝙾𝚛𝚍(a×b)}} called the ordinal product of ordinals {{math|a}}, and {{math|b}}.}}


{{term|⊗}}
{{defn|defn=For cardinals {{math|a}}, and {{math|b}}, {{math|a⊗b≔𝙲𝚛𝚍(a×b)}}, called the cardinal product of cardinals {{math|a}}, and {{math|b}}.}}

{{term|*}}
{{defn|defn=An operation that takes a forcing poset and a name for a forcing poset and produces a new forcing poset.}}

{{term|∞}}
{{defn|defn=The class of all ordinals, or at least something larger than all ordinals}}

{{term|1=<math>\alpha^\beta</math>}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=Cardinal exponentiation}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=Ordinal exponentiation}}

{{term|1=<math>{}^\beta\alpha</math>}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The set of functions from ''β'' to ''α''}}

{{term|→}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=Implies}}
{{defn|no=2|defn={{math|''f'': ''X'' → ''Y''}} means ''f'' is a function from ''X'' to ''Y''.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=The [[ordinary partition symbol]], where {{math|''κ''→(''λ''){{su|p=''n''|b=''m''}}}} means that for every coloring of the ''n''-element subsets of {{mvar|κ}} with ''m'' colors there is a subset of size λ all of whose ''n''-element subsets are the same color.}}

{{term|''f''&prime;''x''}}
{{defn|defn=If there is a unique ''y'' such that ⟨''x'',''y''⟩ is in ''f'' then {{math|{{prime|''f''}}''x''}} is ''y'', otherwise it is the empty set. So if ''f'' is a function and ''x'' is in its domain, then {{math|{{prime|''f''}}''x''}} is ''f''(''x'').}}

{{term|''f''{{pprime}}''X''}}
{{defn|defn={{math|{{pprime|''f''}}''X''}} is the image of a set ''X'' by ''f''. If ''f'' is a function whose domain contains ''X'' this is {{math|{{mset|''f''(''x''):''x''∈''X''}}}}}}

{{term|[ ]}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=''M''[''G''] is the smallest model of ZF containing ''G'' and all elements of ''M''.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[''α'']<sup>''β''</sup> is the set of all subsets of a set ''α'' of cardinality ''β'', or of an ordered set ''α'' of order type ''β''}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=[''x''] is the equivalence class of ''x''}}

{{term|{ } }}
{{defn|no=1|defn={''a'', ''b'', ...} is the set with elements ''a'', ''b'', ...}}
{{defn|no=2|defn={''x'' : ''φ''(''x'')} is the set of ''x'' such that ''φ''(''x'')}}

{{term|⟨ ⟩}}
{{defn|defn=⟨''a'',''b''⟩ is an [[ordered pair]], and similarly for ordered ''n''-tuples}}

{{term|<math>|X|</math>}}
{{defn|defn=The cardinality of a set ''X''}}

{{term|<math>\|\varphi\|</math>}}
{{defn|defn=The value of a formula ''φ'' in some Boolean algebra}}

{{term|⌜''φ''⌝}}
{{defn|defn=⌜''φ''⌝ ([[Quine quotes]], unicode U+231C, U+231D) is the [[Gödel number]] of a formula ''φ''}}

{{term|⊦}}
{{defn|defn={{math|''A''⊦''φ''}} means that the formula ''φ'' follows from the theory ''A''}}

{{term|⊧}}
{{defn|defn={{math|''A''⊧''φ''}} means that the formula ''φ'' holds in the [[model theory|model]] ''A''}}

{{term|⊩}}
{{defn|defn=The [[forcing relation]]}}

{{term|≺}}
{{defn|defn=An [[elementary embedding]]}}

{{term|⊥}}
{{defn|defn=The [[False (logic)|false]] symbol}}
{{defn|defn=''p''⊥''q'' means that ''p'' and ''q'' are incompatible elements of a partial order}}

{{term||term=0#|content={{nobold|{{math|0<sup>#</sup>}}}}}}
{{defn|defn=[[zero sharp]], the set of true formulas about indiscernibles and order-indiscernibles in the constructible universe}}

{{term||term=0†|content={{nobold|{{math|0<sup>†</sup>}}}}}}
{{defn|defn=[[zero dagger]], a certain set of true formulas}}

{{term|2={{tmath|\aleph}}|ℵ}}
{{defn|defn=The Hebrew letter [[aleph]], which indexes the [[aleph number]]s or infinite cardinals {{math|ℵ<sub>''α''</sub>}}}}

{{term|2={{tmath|\beth}}|ב}}
{{defn|defn=The Hebrew letter [[beth (letter)|beth]], which indexes the [[beth number]]s {{math|ב<sub>''α''</sub>}}}}

{{term|2=<math>\gimel</math>|ג}}
{{defn|defn=A serif form of the Hebrew letter [[gimel]], representing the [[gimel function]] <math>\gimel(\kappa)=\kappa^{\operatorname{cf} \kappa}</math>}}

{{term|2={{math|ת}}|ת}}
{{defn|defn=The Hebrew letter [[Taw]], used by Cantor for the [[Tav (number)|class of all cardinal numbers]]}}

{{glossary end}}

==A==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝔞}}
{{defn|defn=The almost disjointness number, the least size of a maximal [[almost disjoint family]] of infinite subsets of ''ω''}}

{{term|A}}
{{defn|defn=The [[Suslin operation]]}}

{{term|absolute}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A statement is called [[Absoluteness (logic)|absolute]] if its truth in some model implies its truth in certain related models}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=Cantor's absolute is a somewhat unclear concept sometimes used to mean the class of all sets}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=Cantor's [[Absolute infinite]] Ω is a somewhat unclear concept related to the class of all ordinals}}

{{term|AC}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=AC is the [[Axiom of choice]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=AC<sub>''ω''</sub> is the [[Axiom of countable choice]]}}

{{term|AD}}
{{defn|defn=The [[axiom of determinacy]]}}

{{term|add}}
{{term|additivity}}
{{defn|defn=The additivity {{math|add(''I'')}} of {{mvar|I}} is the smallest number of sets of {{mvar|I}} with union not in {{mvar|I}}}}

{{term|additively}}
{{defn|defn=An ordinal is called [[additively indecomposable]] if it is not the sum of a finite number of smaller ordinals. These are the same as [[Additively indecomposable ordinal|gamma number]]s or powers of ''ω''. }}

{{term|admissible}}
{{defn|defn=An [[admissible set]] is a model of Kripke–Platek set theory, and an [[admissible ordinal]] is an ordinal α such that ''L''<sub>''α''</sub> is an admissible set}}

{{term|AH}}
{{defn|defn=The [[generalized continuum hypothesis]] states that 2<sup>ℵ<sub>''α''</sub></sup> = ℵ<sub>''α''+1</sub>}}

{{term|aleph}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The Hebrew letter [[aleph|ℵ]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An infinite cardinal}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=The [[aleph function]] taking ordinals to infinite cardinals}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=The [[aleph hypothesis]] is a form of the generalized continuum hypothesis}}

{{term|almost universal}}
{{defn|defn=A class is called [[almost universal]] if every subset of it is contained in some member of it}}

{{term|amenable}}
{{defn|defn=An [[amenable set]] is a set that is a model of Kripke–Platek set theory without the axiom of collection}}

{{term|analytic}}
{{defn|defn=An [[analytic set]] is the continuous image of a Polish space. (This is not the same as an analytical set)}}

{{term|analytical}}
{{defn|defn=The [[analytical hierarchy]] is a hierarchy of subsets of an effective Polish space (such as ''ω''). They are definable by a second-order formula without parameters, and an analytical set is a set in the analytical hierarchy. (This is not the same as an analytic set)}}

{{term|antichain}}
{{defn|defn=An [[antichain]] is a set of pairwise incompatible elements of a poset}}

{{term |1=[[Aczel's anti-foundation axiom|anti-foundation axiom]]}}
{{defn |1=An axiom in set theory that allows for the existence of non-well-founded sets, in contrast to the traditional [[Axiom of regularity|foundation axiom]] which prohibits such sets.}}

{{term|antinomy}}
{{defn|defn=paradox}}

{{term|arithmetic}}
{{defn|defn=The [[ordinal arithmetic]] is arithmetic on [[ordinal number]]s}}
{{defn|defn=The [[cardinal arithmetic]] is arithmetic on [[cardinal number]]s}}

{{term|arithmetical|multi=y}}
{{defn|defn=The [[arithmetical hierarchy]] is a hierarchy of subsets of a Polish space that can be defined by first-order formulas}}

{{term|Aronszajn}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Nachman Aronszajn]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An [[Aronszajn tree]] is an uncountable tree such that all branches and levels are countable. More generally a ''κ''-[[Aronszajn tree]] is a tree of cardinality ''κ'' such that all branches and levels have cardinality less than ''κ''}}

{{term|atom}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=An [[urelement]], something that is not a set but allowed to be an element of a set}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An element of a poset such that any two elements smaller than it are compatible.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A set of positive measure such that every measurable subset has the same measure or measure 0}}

{{term|atomic}}
{{defn|defn=An atomic formula (in set theory) is one of the form ''x''=''y'' or ''x''∈''y''}}

{{term|axiom}}
{{defn|no=|[[Aczel's anti-foundation axiom]] states that every accessible pointed directed graph corresponds to a unique set}}
{{defn|no=|[[AD+]] An extension of the axiom of determinacy}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom F]] states that the class of all ordinals is Mahlo}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of adjunction]] Adjoining a set to another set produces a set}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of amalgamation]] The union of all elements of a set is a set. Same as axiom of union}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of choice]] The product of any set of non-empty sets is non-empty}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of collection]] This can mean either the axiom of replacement or the axiom of separation}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of comprehension]] The class of all sets with a given property is a set. Usually contradictory.}}
{{defn|no=|1=[[Axiom of constructibility]] Any set is constructible, often abbreviated as ''V''=''L''}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of countability]]  Every set is hereditarily countable}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of countable choice]] The product of a countable number of non-empty sets is non-empty}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of dependent choice]] A weak form of the axiom of choice}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of determinacy]] Certain games are determined, in other words one player has a winning strategy}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of elementary sets]] describes the sets with 0, 1, or 2 elements}} 
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of empty set]] The empty set exists}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of extensionality]] or axiom of extent}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of finite choice]] Any product of non-empty finite sets is non-empty}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of foundation]] Same as axiom of regularity}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of global choice]] There is a global choice function}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of heredity]] (any member of a set is a set; used in Ackermann's system.)}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of infinity]] There is an infinite set}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of limitation of size]] A class is a set if and only if it has smaller cardinality than the class of all sets}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of pairing]] Unordered pairs of sets are sets}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of power set]] The powerset of any set is a set}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of projective determinacy]]  Certain games given by projective set are determined, in other words one player has a winning strategy}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of real determinacy]]  Certain games are determined, in other words one player has a winning strategy}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of regularity]] Sets are well founded}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of replacement]] The image of a set under a function is a set. Same as axiom of substitution}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of subsets]] The powerset of a set is a set. Same as axiom of powersets}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of substitution]] The image of a set under a function is a set}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom of union]]  The union of all elements of a set is a set}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom schema of predicative separation]] Axiom of separation for formulas whose quantifiers are bounded}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom schema of replacement]] The image of a set under a function is a set}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom schema of separation]] The elements of a set with some property form a set}}
{{defn|no=|[[Axiom schema of specification]] The elements of a set with some property form a set. Same as axiom schema of separation}}
{{defn|no=|[[Freiling's axiom of symmetry]] is equivalent to the negation of the continuum hypothesis}}
{{defn|no=|[[Martin's axiom]] states very roughly that cardinals less than the cardinality of the continuum behave like ℵ<sub>0</sub>.}}
{{defn|no=|The [[proper forcing axiom]] is a strengthening of Martin's axiom}}

{{glossary end}}

==B==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝔟}}
{{defn|defn=The [[bounding number]], the least size of an unbounded family of sequences of natural numbers}}

{{term|B}}
{{defn|defn=A [[Boolean algebra]]}}

{{term|BA}}
{{defn|defn=[[Baumgartner's axiom]], one of three axioms introduced by Baumgartner.}}

{{term|BACH}}
{{defn|defn=[[Baumgartner's axiom]] plus the continuum hypothesis.}}

{{term|Baire}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[René-Louis Baire]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A subset of a topological space has the [[Baire property]] if it differs from an open set by a meager set}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=The [[Baire space (set theory)|Baire space]] is a topological space whose points are sequences of natural numbers}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=A [[Baire space]] is a topological space such that every intersection of a countable collection of open dense sets is dense}}

{{term|basic set theory}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Naive set theory]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A weak set theory, given by [[Kripke–Platek set theory]] without the axiom of collection. Sometimes also called "rudimentary set theory".<ref>P. Aczel, [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0049237X0871989X The Type Theoretic Interpretation of Constructive Set Theory] (1978)</ref>}}

{{term|BC}}
{{defn|defn=[[Berkeley cardinal]]}}

{{term|BD}}
{{defn|defn=[[Borel determinacy]]}}

{{term|Berkeley cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=A [[Berkeley cardinal]] is a cardinal κ in a model of ZF such that for every transitive set ''M'' that includes κ, there is a nontrivial elementary embedding of ''M'' into ''M'' with critical point below κ.}}

{{term|Bernays}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Paul Bernays]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Bernays–Gödel set theory]] is a set theory with classes}}

{{term|Berry's paradox}}
{{defn|defn=[[Berry's paradox]] considers the smallest positive integer not definable in ten words}}

{{term|beth}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The Hebrew letter [[beth (letter)|ב]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[beth number]] ב<sub>α</sub>}}

{{term|Beth}}
{{defn|defn=[[Evert Willem Beth]], as in [[Beth definability]]}}

{{term|BG}}
{{defn|defn=[[Bernays–Gödel set theory]] without the axiom of choice}}

{{term|BGC}}
{{defn|defn=[[Bernays–Gödel set theory]] with the axiom of choice}}

{{term|boldface}}
{{defn|defn=The [[boldface hierarchy]] is a hierarchy of subsets of a Polish space, definable by second-order formulas with parameters (as opposed to the lightface hierarchy which does not allow parameters). It includes the Borel sets, analytic sets, and projective sets}}

{{term|Boolean algebra}}
{{defn|defn=A [[Boolean algebra]] is a commutative ring such that all elements satisfy ''x''<sup>2</sup>=''x''}}

{{term|Borel}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Émile Borel]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Borel set]] is a set in the smallest sigma algebra containing the open sets}}

{{term|bounding number}}
{{defn|defn=The [[bounding number]] is the least size of an unbounded family of sequences of natural numbers}}

{{term|BP}}
{{defn|defn=[[Baire property]]}}

{{term|BS}}
{{term|BST}}
{{defn|defn=Basic set theory}}

{{term|Burali-Forti}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Cesare Burali-Forti]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Burali-Forti paradox]] states that the ordinal numbers do not form a set}}

{{glossary end}}

==C==
{{glossary}}

{{term|c}}
{{term|𝔠|multi=y}}
{{defn|defn=The [[cardinality of the continuum]]}}

{{term|∁}}
{{defn|defn=Complement of a set}}

{{term|C}}
{{defn|defn=The [[Cantor set]]}}

{{term|cac}}
{{defn|defn=[[countable antichain condition]] (same as the countable chain condition)}}

{{term|Cantor}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Georg Cantor]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Cantor normal form]] of an ordinal is its base ''ω'' expansion.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=[[Cantor's paradox]] says that the powerset of a set is larger than the set, which gives a contradiction when applied to the universal set.}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=The [[Cantor set]], a perfect nowhere dense subset of the real line}}
{{defn|no=5|defn=[[Cantor's absolute infinite]] Ω is something to do with the class of all ordinals}}
{{defn|no=6|defn=[[Cantor's absolute]] is a somewhat unclear concept sometimes used to mean the class of all sets}}
{{defn|no=7|defn=[[Cantor's theorem]] states that the powerset operation increases cardinalities}}

{{term|Card}}
{{defn|defn=The cardinality of a set}}

{{term|[[Cartesian product]]}}
{{defn|defn=The set of all ordered pairs obtained from two sets, where each pair consists of one element from each set.}}

{{term|cardinal}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[cardinal number]] is an [[Ordinal number|ordinal]] with more elements than any smaller ordinal}}

{{term|cardinality}}
{{defn|defn=The number of elements of a set}}

{{term|categorical}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A theory is called [[Categorical theory|categorical]] if all models are isomorphic. This definition is no longer used much, as first-order theories with infinite models are never categorical.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A theory is called [[:fr:Théorie k-catégorique|k-categorical]] if all models of cardinality ''κ'' are isomorphic}}

{{term|category}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A set of first category is the same as a [[meager set]]: a set that is the union of a countable number of nowhere-dense sets, and a set of second category is a set that is not of first category.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A category in the sense of [[category theory]].}}

{{term|ccc}}
{{defn|defn=[[countable chain condition]]}}

{{term|cf}}
{{defn|defn=The [[cofinality]] of an ordinal}}

{{term|CH}}
{{defn|defn=The [[continuum hypothesis]]}}

{{term|chain}}
{{defn|defn=A linearly ordered subset (of a {{gli|poset}})}}

{{term |1=characteristic function}}
{{defn |1=A function that indicates membership of an element in a set, taking the value 1 if the element is in the set and 0 otherwise.}}

{{term |1=choice function}}
{{defn |1=A function that, given a set of non-empty sets, assigns to each set an element from that set. Fundamental in the formulation of the axiom of choice in set theory.}}

{{term |1=choice negation}}
{{defn |1=In logic, an operation that negates the principles underlying the axiom of choice, exploring alternative set theories where the axiom does not hold.}}

{{term |1=choice set}}
{{defn |1=A set constructed from a collection of non-empty sets by selecting one element from each set, related to the concept of a choice function.}}

{{term|cl}}
{{defn|defn=Abbreviation for "closure of" (a set under some collection of operations)}}

{{term|class}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[class (set theory)|class]] is a collection of sets}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=First class ordinals are finite ordinals, and second class ordinals are countable infinite ordinals}}

{{term |1=class comprehension schema}}
{{defn |1=A principle in set theory allowing the formation of classes based on properties or conditions that their members satisfy.}}

{{term|club}}
{{defn|defn=A contraction of "closed unbounded"}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[club set]] is a closed unbounded subset, often of an ordinal}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[club filter]] is the filter of all subsets containing a club set}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=[[Clubsuit]] is a combinatorial principle similar to but weaker than the diamond principle}}

{{term|coanalytic}}
{{defn|defn=A [[coanalytic set]] is the complement of an analytic set}}

{{term|cofinal}}
{{defn|defn=A subset of a poset is called [[cofinal (mathematics)|cofinal]] if every element of the poset is at most some element of the subset.}}

{{term|cof}}
{{defn|defn=cofinality}}

{{term|cofinality}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The [[cofinality]] of a poset (especially an ordinal or cardinal) is the smallest cardinality of a cofinal subset}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The cofinality {{math|cof(''I'')}} of an ideal {{mvar|I}} of subsets of a set ''X'' is the smallest cardinality of a subset ''B'' of {{mvar|I}} such that every element of ''I'' is a subset of something in ''B''.}}

{{term |1=cofinite}}
{{defn |1=Referring to a set whose complement in a larger set is finite, often used in discussions of topology and set theory.}}

{{term|Cohen}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Paul Cohen]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Cohen forcing]] is a method for constructing models of ZFC}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[Cohen algebra]] is a Boolean algebra whose completion is free}}

{{term|Col}}
{{term|collapsing algebra|multi=y}}
{{defn|defn=A [[collapsing algebra]] Col(''κ,λ'') collapses cardinals between ''λ'' and ''κ''}}

{{term |1=[[combinatorial set theory]]}}
{{defn |1=A branch of set theory focusing on the study of combinatorial properties of sets and their implications for the structure of the mathematical universe.}}

{{term |1=compact cardinal}}
{{defn |1=A cardinal number that is uncountable and has the property that any collection of sets of that cardinality has a subcollection of the same cardinality with a non-empty intersection.}}

{{term |1=complement (of a set)}}
{{defn |1=The set containing all elements not in the given set, within a larger set considered as the universe.}}

{{term|complete}}
{{defn|no=1|defn="Complete set" is an old term for "transitive set"}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A theory is called [[Complete theory|complete]] if it assigns a truth value (true or false) to every statement of its language}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=An ideal is called κ-complete if it is closed under the union of less than κ elements}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=A measure is called κ-complete if the union of less than κ measure 0 sets has measure 0}}
{{defn|no=5|defn=A linear order is called complete if every nonempty bounded subset has a least upper bound}}

{{term|Con}}
{{defn|defn=Con(''T'') for a theory ''T'' means ''T'' is consistent}}

{{term|condensation lemma}}
{{defn|defn=Gödel's [[condensation lemma]] says that an elementary submodel of an element ''L''<sub>''α''</sub> of the constructible hierarchy is isomorphic to an element ''L''<sub>''&gamma;''</sub> of the constructible hierarchy}}

{{term|constructible}}
{{defn|defn=A set is called constructible if it is in the [[constructible universe]].}}

{{term|continuum}}
{{defn|defn=The [[continuum (set theory)|continuum]] is the real line or its cardinality}}

{{term |1=[[continuum hypothesis]]}}
{{defn |1=The hypothesis in set theory that there is no set whose cardinality is strictly between that of the integers and the real numbers.}}

{{term |1=continuum many}}
{{defn |1=An informal way of saying that a set has the cardinality of the continuum, the size of the set of real numbers.}}

{{term |1=continuum problem}}
{{defn |1=The problem of determining the possible cardinalities of infinite sets, including whether the continuum hypothesis is true.}}

{{term|core}}
{{defn|defn=A [[core model]] is a special sort of inner model generalizing the constructible universe}}

{{term |1=countable}}
{{defn |1=A set is countable if it is finite or if its elements can be put into a one-to-one correspondence with the natural numbers.}}

{{term|countable antichain condition}}
{{defn|defn=A term used for the [[countable chain condition]] by authors who think terminology should be logical}}

{{term |1=countable cardinal}}
{{defn |1=A cardinal number that represents the size of a countable set, typically the cardinality of the set of natural numbers.}}

{{term|countable chain condition}}
{{defn|defn=The [[countable chain condition]] (ccc) for a poset states that every antichain is countable}}

{{term |1=countable ordinal}}
{{defn |1=An ordinal number that represents the order type of a well-ordered set that is countable, including all finite ordinals and the first infinite ordinal, <math>\omega</math>.}}

{{term |1=countably infinite}}
{{defn |1=A set that has the same cardinality as the set of natural numbers, meaning its elements can be listed in a sequence without end.}}

{{term|cov(''I'')}}
{{term|covering number}}
{{defn|defn=The covering number {{math|cov(''I'')}} of an ideal {{mvar|I}} of subsets of ''X'' is the smallest number of sets in {{mvar|I}} whose union is ''X''.}}

{{term|critical}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The critical point κ of an elementary embedding ''j''  is the smallest ordinal κ  with {{itco|''j''}}(''κ'') > ''κ''}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A critical number of a function ''j'' is an ordinal κ with {{itco|''j''}}(''κ'') = ''κ''. This is almost the opposite of the first meaning.}}

{{term|CRT}}
{{defn|defn=The critical point of something}}

{{term|CTM}}
{{defn|defn=[[Countable transitive model]]}}

{{term|cumulative hierarchy}}
{{defn|defn=A [[cumulative hierarchy]] is a sequence of sets indexed by ordinals that satisfies certain conditions and whose union is used as a model of set theory}}

{{glossary end}}

==D==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝔡}}
{{defn|defn=The [[dominating number]] of a poset}}

{{term|DC}}
{{defn|defn=The [[axiom of dependent choice]]}}

{{term|Dedekind}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Richard Dedekind]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Dedekind-infinite set]] is a set that can be put into a one-to-one correspondence with one of its proper subsets, indicating a type of infinity; a Dedekind-finite set is a set that is not Dedekind-infinite. (These are also spelled without the hyphen, as "Dedekind finite" and "Dedekind infinite".)}}

{{term|def}}
{{defn|defn=The set of definable subsets of a set}}

{{term|definable}}
{{defn|defn=A subset of a set is called [[definable set]] if it is the collection of elements satisfying a sentence in some given language}}

{{term|delta}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[delta number]] is an ordinal of the form ''ω<sup>ω<sup>α</sup></sup>''}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[delta system]], also called a sunflower, is a collection of sets such that any two distinct sets have intersection ''X'' for some fixed set ''X''}}

{{term|denumerable}}
{{defn|defn=countable and infinite}}

{{term |1=dependent choice}}
{{defn |1=See [[Axiom of dependent choice]]}}

{{term |1=determinateness}}
{{defn |1=See [[Axiom of extensionality]]}}

{{term|Df}}
{{defn|defn=The set of definable subsets of a set}}

{{term |1=diagonal argument}}
{{defn |1=[[Cantor's diagonal argument]]}}

{{term |1=[[Cantor's diagonal argument|diagonalization]]}}
{{defn |1=A method used in set theory and logic to construct a set or sequence that is not in a given collection by ensuring it differs from each member of the collection in at least one element.}}

{{term|diagonal intersection}}
{{defn|defn=If <math>\displaystyle\langle X_\alpha \mid \alpha<\delta\rangle</math>
is a sequence of subsets of an ordinal <math>\displaystyle\delta</math>, then the [[diagonal intersection]] <math>\displaystyle\Delta_{\alpha<\delta} X_\alpha,</math>
is
<math>\displaystyle\{\beta<\delta\mid\beta\in \bigcap_{\alpha<\beta} X_\alpha\}.</math>}}

{{term|diamond principle}}
{{defn|defn=Jensen's [[diamond principle]] states that there are sets {{math|''A<sub>α</sub>''⊆''α''}} for ''α''<''ω''<sub>1</sub> such that for any subset ''A'' of ''ω''<sub>1</sub> the set of ''α'' with {{math|1=''A''∩''α'' = ''A<sub>α</sub>''}} is stationary in ''ω''<sub>1</sub>.}}

{{term |1=discrete}}
{{defn |1=A property of a set or space that consists of distinct, separate elements or points, with no intermediate values.}}

{{term |1=disjoint}}
{{defn |1=Referring to sets that have no element in common, i.e., their intersection is empty.}}

{{term|dom}}
{{defn|defn=The domain of a function}}

{{term|DST}}
{{defn|defn=[[Descriptive set theory]]}}

{{glossary end}}

==E==
{{glossary}}
{{term|''E''}}
{{defn|defn=''E''(''X'') is the membership relation of the set ''X''}}

{{term|Easton's theorem}}
{{defn|defn=[[Easton's theorem]] describes the possible behavior of the powerset function on regular cardinals}}

{{term|EATS}}
{{defn|defn=The statement "every Aronszajn tree is special"}}

{{term |1=effectively decidable set}}
{{defn |1=A set for which there exists an algorithm that can determine, for any given element, whether it belongs to the set.}}

{{term |1=effectively enumerable set}}
{{defn |1=A set whose members can be listed or enumerated by some algorithm, even if the list is potentially infinite.}}

{{term |1=[[Element (mathematics)|element]]}}
{{defn |1=An individual object or member of a set.}}

{{term|elementary}}
{{defn|defn=An [[elementary embedding]] is a function preserving all properties describable in the language of set theory}}

{{term |1=[[empty set]]}}
{{defn |1=The unique set that contains no elements, denoted by <math>\emptyset</math>.}}

{{term |1=empty set axiom}}
{{defn |1=See [[Axiom of empty set]].}}

{{term |1=enumerable set}}
{{defn |1=A set whose elements can be put into a one-to-one correspondence with the set of natural numbers, making it countable.}}

{{term |1=enumeration}}
{{defn |1=The process of listing or counting elements in a set, especially for countable sets.}}

{{term|epsilon}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=An [[epsilon number (mathematics)|epsilon number]] is an ordinal α such that ''α''=''ω<sup>α</sup>''}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=Epsilon zero (''&epsilon;''<sub>0</sub>) is the smallest [[Epsilon numbers (mathematics)|epsilon number]]}}

{{term |1=equicardinal}}
{{defn |1=Synonym of 
[[Equinumerosity|equinumerous]]}}

{{term |1=[[Equinumerosity|equinumerous]]}}
{{defn |1=Having the same cardinal number or number of elements, used to describe two sets that can be put into a one-to-one correspondence.}}

{{term |1=equipollent}}
{{defn |1=Synonym of [[Equinumerosity|equinumerous]]}}

{{term |1=equipotent}}
{{defn |1= Synonym of
[[Equinumerosity|equinumerous]]}}

{{term |1=equivalence class}}
{{defn |1=A subset within a set, defined by an equivalence relation, where every element in the subset is equivalent to each other under that relation.}}

{{term|Erdos}}
{{term|Erdős|multi=y}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Paul Erdős]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An [[Erdős cardinal]] is a large cardinal satisfying a certain partition condition. (They are also called partition cardinals.)}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=The [[Erdős–Rado theorem]] extends Ramsey's theorem to infinite cardinals}}

{{term|ethereal cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=An [[ethereal cardinal]] is a type of large cardinal similar in strength to subtle cardinals}}

{{term|[[Euler diagram]]}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A graphical representation of the logical relationships between sets, using overlapping circles to illustrate intersections, unions, and complements of sets.}}

{{term|extender}}
{{defn|defn=An [[Extender (set theory)|extender]] is a system of ultrafilters encoding an elementary embedding}}

{{term|extendible cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=A cardinal ''κ'' is called [[extendible cardinal|extendible]] if for all ''η'' there is a nontrivial elementary embedding of ''V''<sub>''κ''+''η''</sub> into some V<sub>λ</sub> with critical point ''κ''}}

{{term|extension}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=If ''R'' is a relation on a class then the extension of an element ''y'' is the class of ''x'' such that ''xRy''}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An extension of a model is a larger model containing it}}

{{term|extensional}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A relation ''R'' on a class is called extensional if every element ''y'' of the class is determined by its extension}}

{{defn|no=2|defn=A class is called extensional if the relation ∈ on the class is extensional}}

{{glossary end}}

==F==
{{glossary}}

{{term|F}}
{{defn|defn=An ''F''<sub>σ</sub> is a union of a countable number of closed sets}}

{{term|Feferman–Schütte ordinal}}
{{defn|defn=The [[Feferman–Schütte ordinal]] Γ<sub>0</sub> is in some sense the smallest impredicative ordinal}}

{{term|filter}}
{{defn|defn=A [[filter (mathematics)|filter]] is a non-empty subset of a poset that is downward-directed and upwards-closed}}

{{term|finite intersection property}}
{{term|FIP|multi=y}}
{{defn|defn=The [[finite intersection property]], abbreviated FIP, says that the intersection of any finite number of elements of a set is non-empty}}

{{term|first}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A set of [[meagre set|first category]] is the same as a meager set: one that is the union of a countable number of nowhere-dense sets.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An ordinal of the first class is a finite ordinal}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=An ordinal of the first kind is a successor ordinal}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=[[First-order logic]] allows quantification over elements of a model, but not over subsets}}

{{term|Fodor}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Géza Fodor (mathematician)|Géza Fodor]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Fodor's lemma]] states that a regressive function on a regular uncountable cardinal is constant on a stationary subset.}}

{{term|forcing}}
{{defn|defn=[[Forcing (mathematics)]] is a method of adjoining a generic filter ''G'' of a poset ''P'' to a model of set theory ''M'' to obtain a new model ''M''[''G'']}}

{{term|formula}}
{{defn|defn=Something formed from atomic formulas ''x''=''y'', ''x''∈''y'' using ∀∃∧∨¬}}

{{term |1=foundation axiom}}
{{defn |1=See [[Axiom of foundation]]}}

{{term|Fraenkel}}
{{defn|defn=[[Abraham Fraenkel]]}}

{{glossary end}}

==G==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝖌}}
{{defn|defn=The groupwise density number}}

{{term|G}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[generic ultrafilter]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A ''G''<sub>''δ''</sub> is a countable intersection of open sets}}

{{term|gamma number}}
{{defn|defn=A [[Additively indecomposable ordinal|gamma number]] is an ordinal of the form ''ω<sup>α</sup>''}}

{{term|GCH}}
{{defn|defn=[[Generalized continuum hypothesis]]}}

{{term|generalized continuum hypothesis}}
{{defn|defn=The [[generalized continuum hypothesis]] states that 2<sup>א<sub>''α''</sub></sup> = א<sub>''α''+1</sub>}}

{{term|generic}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[generic filter]] of a poset ''P'' is a filter that intersects all dense subsets of ''P'' that are contained in some model ''M''.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[generic extension]] of a model ''M'' is a model ''M''[''G''] for some generic filter ''G''.}}

{{term|gimel}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The Hebrew letter [[gimel]] <math>\gimel</math>}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[gimel function]]  <math>\gimel(\kappa)=\kappa^{\text{cf}(\kappa)}</math>}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=The [[gimel hypothesis]] states that <math>\gimel(\kappa)=\max(2^{\text{cf}(\kappa)},\kappa^+)</math>}}

{{term|global choice}}
{{defn|defn=The [[axiom of global choice]] says there is a well ordering of the class of all sets}}

{{term |1=global well-ordering}}
{{defn |1=Another name for the [[axiom of global choice]]}}

{{term |1=[[greatest lower bound]]}}
{{defn |1=The largest value that serves as a lower bound for a set in a partially ordered set, also known as the infimum.}}

{{term|Godel}}
{{term|Gödel|multi=y}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Kurt Gödel]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Gödel number]] is a number assigned to a formula}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=The [[Gödel's constructible universe|Gödel universe]] is another name for the constructible universe}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=[[Gödel's incompleteness theorems]] show that sufficiently powerful consistent recursively enumerable theories cannot be complete}}
{{defn|no=5|defn=[[Gödel's completeness theorem]] states that consistent first-order theories have models}}

{{glossary end}}

==H==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝔥}}
{{defn|defn=The distributivity number}}

{{term|H}}
{{defn|defn=Abbreviation for "hereditarily"}}

{{term|term=Hκ|content=''H''<sub>''κ''</sub>}}
{{term|''H''(''κ'')}}
{{defn|defn=The set of sets that are hereditarily of cardinality less than κ}}

{{term|Hartogs}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Friedrich Hartogs]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Hartogs number]] of a set ''X'' is the least ordinal α such that there is no injection from α into ''X''.}}

{{term|Hausdorff}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Felix Hausdorff]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Hausdorff gap]] is a gap in the ordered set of growth rates of sequences of integers, or in a similar ordered set}}

{{term|HC}}
{{defn|defn=The set of [[hereditarily countable]] sets}}

{{term|hereditarily}}
{{defn|defn=If ''P'' is a property the a set is hereditarily ''P'' if all elements of its transitive closure have property ''P''. Examples:
[[Hereditarily countable set]]
[[Hereditarily finite set]]}}

{{term|Hessenberg}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Gerhard Hessenberg]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Hessenberg sum]] and [[Hessenberg product]] are commutative operations on ordinals}}

{{term|HF}}
{{defn|defn=The set of [[hereditarily finite set]]s}}

{{term|Hilbert}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[David Hilbert]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Hilbert's paradox]] states that a Hotel with an infinite number of rooms can accommodate extra guests even if it is full}}

{{term|HS}}
{{defn|defn=The class of [[hereditarily symmetric set]]s}}
{{term|HOD}}
{{defn|defn=The class of [[hereditarily ordinal definable]] sets}}

{{term|huge cardinal}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[huge cardinal]] is a cardinal number κ such that there exists an elementary embedding ''j'' : ''V'' → ''M'' with critical point κ from ''V'' into a transitive inner model ''M'' containing  all sequences of length {{itco|''j''}}(''κ'') whose elements are in ''M''}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An ω-huge cardinal is a large cardinal related to the {{math|''I''<sub>1</sub>}} [[rank-into-rank]] axiom}}

{{term|hyperarithmetic}}
{{defn|defn=A [[hyperarithmetic set]] is a subset of the natural numbers given by a transfinite extension of the notion of arithmetic set}}

{{term|hyperinaccessible}}
{{term|hyper-inaccessible|multi=y}}
{{defn|no=1|defn="Hyper-inaccessible cardinal" usually means a [[inaccessible cardinal|1-inaccessible cardinal]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn="Hyper-inaccessible cardinal" sometimes means a cardinal ''&kappa;'' that is a '''&kappa;''-inaccessible cardinal}}
{{defn|no=3|defn="Hyper-inaccessible cardinal" occasionally means a [[Mahlo cardinal]]}}

{{term|hyper-Mahlo}}
{{defn|defn=A [[hyper-Mahlo cardinal]] is a cardinal ''&kappa;'' that is a ''&kappa;''-Mahlo cardinal}}

{{term |1=[[hyperset]]}}
{{defn |1=A set that can contain itself as a member or is defined in terms of a circular or self-referential structure, used in the study of [[Non-well-founded set theory|non-well-founded set theories]].}}

{{term|hyperverse}}
{{defn|defn=The [[hyperverse]] is the set of countable transitive models of ZFC}}

{{glossary end}}

==I==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝔦}}
{{defn|defn=The independence number}}

{{term|I0, I1, I2, I3}}
{{defn|defn=The [[rank-into-rank]] large cardinal axioms}}

{{term|ideal}}
{{defn|defn=An ideal in the sense of [[ring theory]], usually of a [[Boolean algebra]], especially the Boolean algebra of subsets of a set}}

{{term|iff}}
{{defn|defn=if and only if}}

{{term|improper}}
:See proper, below. 

{{term|inaccessible cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=A (weakly or strongly) [[inaccessible cardinal]] is a regular uncountable cardinal that is a (weak or strong) limit}}

{{term|indecomposable ordinal}}
{{defn|defn=An [[indecomposable ordinal]] is a nonzero ordinal that is not the sum of two smaller ordinals, or equivalently an  ordinal of the form ''ω<sup>α</sup>'' or a [[Additively indecomposable ordinal|gamma number]].}}

{{term|independence number}}
{{defn|defn=The independence number 𝔦 is the smallest possible cardinality of a maximal independent family of subsets of a countable infinite set}}

{{term|indescribable cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=An [[indescribable cardinal]] is a type of large cardinal that cannot be described in terms of smaller ordinals using a certain language}}

{{term|individual}}
{{defn|defn=Something with no elements, either the empty set or an [[urelement]] or atom}}

{{term|indiscernible}}
{{defn|defn=A [[set of indiscernibles]] is a set {{mvar|I}} of ordinals such that two increasing finite sequences of elements of {{mvar|I}} have the same first-order properties}}

{{term|inductive}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=An [[inductive set]] is a set that can be generated from a base set by repeatedly applying a certain operation, such as the set of natural numbers generated from the number 0 by the successor operation.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An inductive definition is a definition that specifies how to construct members of a set based on members already known to be in the set, often used for defining recursively defined sequences, functions, and structures.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A poset is called inductive if every non-empty ordered subset has an upper bound}}

{{term |1=infinity axiom}}
{{defn |1=See [[Axiom of infinity]].}}

{{term |1=[[inner model]]}}
{{defn |1=A model of set theory that is constructed within Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory and contains all ordinals of the universe, serving to explore properties of larger set-theoretic universes from a contained perspective.}}

{{term|ineffable cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=An [[ineffable cardinal]] is a type of large cardinal related to the generalized Kurepa hypothesis whose consistency strength lies between that of subtle cardinals and remarkable cardinals}}

{{term|inner model}}
{{defn|defn=An [[inner model]] is a transitive model of ZF containing all ordinals}}

{{term|Int}}
{{defn|defn=Interior of a subset of a topological space}}

{{term |1=integers}}
{{defn |1=The set of whole numbers including positive, negative, and zero, denoted by {{mathbb|Z}}.}}

{{term|internal}}
{{defn|defn=An archaic term for extensional (relation)}}

{{term |1=intersection}}
{{defn |1=The set containing all elements that are members of two or more sets, denoted by <math>A \cap B</math> for sets {{mvar|A}} and {{mvar|B}}.}}

{{term |1=iterative conception of set}}
{{defn |1=A philosophical and mathematical notion that sets are formed by iteratively collecting together objects into a new object, a set, which can then itself be included in further sets.}}

{{glossary end}}

==J==
{{glossary}}

{{term|''j''}}
{{defn|defn=An [[elementary embedding]]}}

{{term|J}}
{{defn|defn=Levels of the [[Jensen hierarchy]]}}

{{term|Jensen}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Ronald Jensen]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Jensen hierarchy]] is a variation of the constructible hierarchy}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=[[Jensen's covering theorem]] states that if 0<sup>#</sup> does not exist then every uncountable set of ordinals is contained in a constructible set of the same cardinality}}

{{term |1=[[Join and meet|join]]}}
{{defn |1=In logic and mathematics, particularly in lattice theory, the join of a set of elements is the least upper bound or supremum of those elements, representing their union in the context of set operations or the least element that is greater than or equal to each of them in a partial order.}}

{{term|Jónsson}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Bjarni Jónsson]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Jónsson cardinal]] is a large cardinal such that  for every function {{itco|''f''}}: [''κ'']<sup><''ω''</sup> → ''κ'' there is a set ''H'' of order type κ such that for each ''n'', ''f'' restricted to ''n''-element subsets of ''H'' omits at least one value in ''κ''.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[Jónsson function]] is a function <math>f:[x]^\omega\to x</math> with the property that, for any subset ''y'' of ''x'' with the same [[cardinality]] as ''x'', the restriction of {{mvar|f}} to <math>[y]^\omega</math> has image {{mvar|x}}.}}

{{glossary end}}

==K==
{{glossary}}

{{term|Kelley}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[John L. Kelley]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Morse–Kelley set theory]] (also called Kelley–Morse set theory), a set theory with classes}}

{{term|KH}}
{{defn|defn=[[Kurepa's hypothesis]]}}

{{term|kind}}
{{defn|defn=Ordinals of the first kind are successor ordinals, and ordinals of the second kind are limit ordinals or 0}}

{{term|KM}}
{{defn|defn=[[Morse–Kelley set theory]]}}

{{term|Kleene–Brouwer ordering}}
{{defn|defn=The [[Kleene–Brouwer ordering]] is a total order on the finite sequences of ordinals}}

{{term |1=[[Kleene hierarchy]]}}
{{defn |1=A classification of sets of natural numbers or strings based on the complexity of the predicates defining them, using Kleene's arithmetical hierarchy in recursion theory.}}

{{term |1=[[Kőnig's lemma|König's lemma]]}}
{{defn |1=A result in [[graph theory]] and [[combinatorics]] stating that every infinite, finitely branching tree has an infinite path, used in proofs of various mathematical and logical theorems. It is equivalent to the [[axiom of dependent choice]].}}

{{term |1=[[König's paradox]]}}
{{defn |1=A paradox in set theory and combinatorics that arises from incorrect assumptions about infinite sets and their cardinalities, related to König's theorem on the sums and products of cardinals.}}

{{term|KP}}
{{defn|defn=[[Kripke–Platek set theory]]}}

{{term|Kripke}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Saul Kripke]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Kripke–Platek set theory]] consists roughly of the predicative parts of set theory}}

{{term |1=Kuratowski}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Kazimierz Kuratowski]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Kuratowski ordered pair]] is a definition of an [[ordered pair]] using only set theoretical concepts, specifically, the ordered pair (a, b) is defined as the set {{a}, {a, b}}.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn="[[Kuratowski-Zorn lemma]]" is an alternative name for [[Zorn's lemma]]}}

{{term|Kurepa}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Đuro Kurepa]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Kurepa hypothesis]] states that Kurepa trees exist}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[Kurepa tree]] is a [[tree (set theory)|tree]] (''T'',&nbsp;<) of height <math>\omega_1</math>, each of whose levels is countable, with at least <math>\aleph_2</math> branches}}

{{glossary end}}

==L==
{{glossary}}

{{term|L}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=''L'' is the [[constructible universe]], and ''L''<sub>α</sub> is the hierarchy of [[constructible universe|constructible sets]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=''L''<sub>κλ</sub> is an [[infinitary language]]}}

{{term|large cardinal}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[large cardinal]] is type of cardinal whose existence cannot be proved in ZFC.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A large large cardinal is a large cardinal that is not compatible with the axiom ''V''=''L''}}

{{term |1=[[Lattice (order)|lattice]]}}
{{defn |1=A partially ordered set in which any two elements have a unique supremum (least upper bound) and an infimum (greatest lower bound), used in various areas of mathematics and logic.}}

{{term|Laver}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Richard Laver]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Laver function]] is a function related to supercompact cardinals that takes ordinals to sets}}

{{term |1=[[least upper bound]]}}
{{defn |1=The smallest element in a partially ordered set that is greater than or equal to every element in a subset of that set, also known as the supremum.}}

{{term|Lebesgue}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Henri Lebesgue]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Lebesgue measure]] is a complete translation-invariant measure on the real line}}

{{term |left-narrow}}
{{defn |1=A partially ordered set, (α,≤) in which for all b in α, {c:c∈α∧c≤b}
(the down-set of b) is a set.}}

{{term|LEM}}
{{defn|defn=[[Law of the excluded middle]]}}

{{term|Lévy}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Azriel Lévy]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Lévy collapse]] is a way of destroying cardinals}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=The [[Lévy hierarchy]] classifies formulas in terms of the number of alternations of unbounded quantifiers}}

{{term|lightface}}
{{defn|defn=The [[lightface]] classes are collections of subsets of an effective Polish space definable by second-order formulas without parameters (as opposed to the boldface hierarchy that allows parameters). They include the arithmetical, hyperarithmetical, and analytical sets}}

{{term|limit}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A (weak) [[limit cardinal]] is a cardinal, usually assumed to be nonzero, that is not the successor κ<sup>+</sup> of another cardinal κ}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A strong [[limit cardinal]] is a cardinal, usually assumed to be nonzero, larger than the powerset of any smaller cardinal}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[limit ordinal]] is an ordinal, usually assumed to be nonzero, that is not the successor α+1 of another ordinal α}}

{{term |1=[[Limitation of size|limitation-of-size conception of set]]}}
{{defn |1=A conception that defines sets in such a way as to avoid certain paradoxes by excluding collections that are too large to be sets.}}

{{term|limited}}
{{defn|defn=A limited quantifier is the same as a [[bounded quantifier]]}}

{{term|LM}}
{{defn|defn=[[Lebesgue measure]]}}

{{term|local}}
{{defn|defn=A property of a set ''x'' is called local if it has the form ∃δ ''V''<sub>δ</sub>⊧ φ(''x'') for some formula φ}}

{{term|LOTS}}
{{defn|defn=Linearly ordered topological space}}

{{term|Löwenheim}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Leopold Löwenheim]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Löwenheim–Skolem theorem]] states that if a first-order theory has an infinite model then it has a model of any given infinite cardinality}}

{{term |1=[[lower bound]]}}
{{defn |1=An element of a partially ordered set that is less than or equal to every element of a given subset of the set, providing a minimum standard or limit for comparison.}}

{{term|LST}}
{{defn|defn=The language of set theory (with a single binary relation ∈)}}

{{glossary end}}

==M==
{{glossary}}
{{term|''m''}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A measure}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A natural number}}

{{term|𝔪}}
{{defn|defn=The smallest cardinal at which [[Martin's axiom]] fails}}

{{term|M}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A model of ZF set theory}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=''M''<sub>α</sub> is an old symbol for the level ''L''<sub>α</sub> of the constructible universe}}

{{term|MA}}
{{defn|defn=[[Martin's axiom]]}}

{{term|MAD}}
{{defn|defn=Maximally Almost Disjoint}}

{{term|Mac Lane}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Saunders Mac Lane]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Mac Lane set theory]] is Zermelo set theory with the axiom of separation restricted to formulas with bounded quantifiers}}

{{term|Mahlo}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Paul Mahlo]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Mahlo cardinal]] is an inaccessible cardinal such that the set of inaccessible cardinals less than it is stationary}}

{{term|Martin}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Donald A. Martin]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Martin's axiom]] for a cardinal κ states that for any partial order ''P'' satisfying the countable chain condition and any family ''D'' of dense sets in ''P'' of cardinality at most κ, there is a filter ''F'' on ''P'' such that {{math|{{itco|''F''}} ∩ {{itco|''d''}}}} is non-empty for every ''d'' in ''D''}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=[[Martin's maximum]] states that if ''D'' is a collection of <math>\aleph_1</math> dense subsets of a notion of forcing that preserves stationary subsets of ω<sub>1</sub>, then there is a ''D''-generic filter}}

{{term|meager}}
{{term|meagre|multi=y}}
{{defn|defn=A [[meager set]] is one that is the union of a countable number of nowhere-dense sets. Also called a set of first category.}}

{{term|measure}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A measure on a [[Sigma-algebra|&sigma;-algebra]] of subsets of a set}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[probability measure]] on the algebra of all subsets of some set}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A measure on the algebra of all subsets of a set, taking values 0 and 1}}

{{term|measurable cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=A [[measurable cardinal]]  is a cardinal number ''κ'' such that there exists a ''κ''-additive, non-trivial, 0-1-valued measure on the power set of ''κ''. Most (but not all) authors add the condition that it should be uncountable}}

{{term |1=[[Join and meet|meet]]}}
{{defn |1=In lattice theory, the operation that combines two elements to produce their greatest lower bound, analogous to intersection in set theory.}}

{{term |1=member}}
{{defn |1=An individual [[Element (mathematics)|element of a set]].}}

{{term |1=membership}}
{{defn |1=The relation between an [[Element (mathematics)|element]] and a set in which the element is included within the set.}}

{{term|mice}}
{{defn|defn=Plural of {{gli|mouse}}}}

{{term|Milner–Rado paradox}}
{{defn|defn=The [[Milner–Rado paradox]] states that every ordinal number ''α'' less than the successor ''κ''<sup>+</sup> of some cardinal number ''κ'' can be written as the union of sets {{tmath|X_1,X_2,...}} where {{tmath|X_n}} is of order type at most ''κ<sup>n</sup>'' for n a positive integer.}}

{{term|MK}}
{{defn|defn=[[Morse–Kelley set theory]]}}

{{term|MM}}
{{defn|defn=[[Martin's maximum]]}}

{{term|morass}}
{{defn|defn=A [[morass (set theory)|morass]] is a tree with ordinals associated to the nodes and some further structure, satisfying some rather complicated axioms.}}

{{term|Morse}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Anthony Morse]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Morse–Kelley set theory]], a set theory with classes}}

{{term|Mostowski}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Andrzej Mostowski]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Mostowski collapse]] is a transitive class associated to a well founded extensional set-like relation.}}

{{term|mouse}}
{{defn|defn=A certain kind of structure used in constructing core models; see [[mouse (set theory)]]}}

{{term|multiplicative axiom}}
{{defn|defn=An old name for the [[axiom of choice]]}}

{{term |1=[[multiset]]}}
{{defn |1=A generalization of a set that allows multiple occurrences of its elements, often used in mathematics and computer science to model collections with repetitions.}}

{{glossary end}}

==N==
{{glossary}}

{{term|N}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The set of [[Natural number|natural numbers]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Baire space (set theory)|Baire space]] ''ω<sup>ω</sup>''}}

{{term |1=naïve comprehension schema}}
{{defn |1=An unrestricted principle in set theory allowing the formation of sets based on any property or condition, leading to paradoxes such as Russell's paradox in naïve set theory.}}

{{term|naive set theory}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Naive set theory]] can mean set theory developed non-rigorously without axioms}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=Naive set theory can mean the inconsistent theory with the axioms of extensionality and comprehension}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=[[Naive Set Theory (book)|Naive set theory]] is an introductory book on set theory by Halmos}}

{{term|natural}}
{{defn|defn=The natural sum and natural product of ordinals are the [[Hessenberg sum]] and product}}

{{term|NCF}}
{{defn|defn=Near Coherence of Filters}}

{{term|no-classes theory}}
{{defn|defn=A theory due to [[Bertrand Russell]], and used in his ''[[Principia Mathematica]]'', according to which [[Set (mathematics)|sets]] can be reduced to certain kinds of [[propositional function]] formulae. (In Russell's time, the distinction between "class" and "set" had not been developed yet, and Russell used the word "class" in his writings, hence the name "no-class" or "no-classes" theory is retained for this historical reason, although the theory refers to what are now called sets.)<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bostock |first=David |title=Russell's logical atomism |date=2012 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-965144-3 |location=Oxford}}</ref>
}}

{{term|non}}
{{defn|defn={{math|non(''I'')}} is the uniformity of {{mvar|I}}, the smallest cardinality of a subset of ''X'' not in the ideal {{mvar|I}} of subsets of ''X''}}

{{term|nonstat}}
{{term|nonstationary}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A subset of an ordinal is called nonstationary if it is not stationary, in other words if its complement contains a club set}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The '''nonstationary ideal''' {{math|''I''<sub>''NS''</sub>}} is the ideal of nonstationary sets}}

{{term|normal}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[normal function]] is a continuous strictly increasing function from ordinals to ordinals}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[normal filter]] or normal measure on an ordinal is a filter or measure closed under [[diagonal intersection]]s}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=The [[Cantor normal form]] of an ordinal is its base ω expansion.}}

{{term|NS}}
{{defn|defn=Nonstationary}}

{{term|null}}
{{defn|defn=German for zero, occasionally used in terms such as "aleph null" (aleph zero) or "null set" (empty set)}}

{{term|number class}}
{{defn|defn=The first number class consists of finite ordinals, and the second number class consists of countable ordinals.}}

{{glossary end}}

==O==
{{glossary}}

{{term|OCA}}
{{defn|defn=The [[open coloring axiom]]}}

{{term|OD}}
{{defn|defn=The [[ordinal definable set]]s}}

{{term|Omega logic}}
{{defn|defn=[[Ω-logic]] is a form of logic introduced by [[Hugh Woodin]]}}

{{term|On}}
{{defn|defn=The class of all ordinals}}

{{term |1=[[order type]]}}
{{defn |1=A concept in set theory and logic that categorizes well-ordered sets by their structure, such that two sets have the same order type if there is a bijective function between them that preserves order.}}

{{term|ordinal}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=An ordinal is the order type of a well-ordered set, usually represented by a [[von Neumann ordinal]], a transitive set well ordered by ∈.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An [[ordinal definable]] set is a set that can be defined by a first-order formula with ordinals as parameters}}

{{term|ot}}
{{defn|defn=Abbreviation for "order type of"}}

{{glossary end}}

==P==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝔭}}
{{defn|defn=The [[pseudo-intersection number]], the smallest cardinality of a family of infinite subsets of ω that has the [[strong finite intersection property]] but has no infinite [[pseudo-intersection]].}}

{{term|''P''}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The {{gli|powerset}} function}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A {{gli|poset}}}}

{{term|pairing function}}
{{defn|defn=A [[pairing function]] is a bijection from ''X''×''X'' to ''X'' for some set ''X''}}

{{term |1=pairwise disjoint}}
{{defn |1=A property of a collection of sets where each pair of sets in the collection has no elements in common.}}

{{term|pantachie}}
{{term|pantachy|multi=y}}
{{defn|defn=A [[pantachy]] is a maximal chain of a poset}}

{{term|paradox}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Berry's paradox]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Burali-Forti's paradox]]}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=[[Cantor's paradox]]}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=[[Hilbert's paradox]]}}
{{defn|no=5|defn=[[König's paradox]]}}
{{defn|no=6|defn=[[Milner–Rado paradox]]}}
{{defn|no=7|defn=[[Richard's paradox]]}}
{{defn|no=8|defn=[[Russell's paradox]]}}
{{defn|no=9|defn=[[Skolem's paradox]]}}

{{term |1=paradox of denotation}}
{{defn |1=A paradox that uses definite descriptions in an essential way, such as [[Berry's paradox]], [[König's paradox]], and [[Richard's paradox]].<ref name="CookDictionary">{{Cite book |last=Cook |first=Roy T. |date=2009-03-20 |title=A Dictionary of Philosophical Logic |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1515/9780748631971 |doi=10.1515/9780748631971|isbn=978-0-7486-3197-1 }}</ref>}}

{{term|partial order}}
{{defn|defn=A transitive antisymmetric, or transitive symmetric relation on a set; see [[partially ordered set]].}}

{{term |1=[[Partition of a set|partition]]}}
{{defn |1=A division of a set into disjoint subsets whose union is the entire set, with no element being left out.}}

{{term|partition cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=An alternative name for an [[Erdős cardinal]]}}

{{term|PCF}}
{{defn|defn=Abbreviation for "possible cofinalities", used in [[PCF theory]]}}

{{term|PD}}
{{defn|defn=The axiom of [[projective determinacy]]}}

{{term|perfect set}}
{{defn|defn=A [[perfect set]] is a subset of a topological set equal to its derived set}}

{{term |1=permutation}}
{{defn |1=A rearrangement of the elements of a set or sequence, where the structure of the set changes but the elements do not.}}

{{term|permutation model}}
{{defn|defn=A [[permutation model]] of ZFA is constructed using a group}}

{{term|PFA}}
{{defn|defn=The [[proper forcing axiom]]}}

{{term|PM}}
{{defn|defn=The hypothesis that all projective subsets of the reals are Lebesgue measurable}}

{{term|po}}
{{defn|defn=An abbreviation for "partial order" or "poset"}}

{{term|poset}}
{{defn|defn=A set with a [[partial order]]}}

{{term |1=[[positive set theory]]}}
{{defn |1=A variant of set theory that includes a universal set and possibly other non-standard axioms, focusing on what can be constructed or defined positively.}}

{{term|Polish space}}
{{defn|defn=A [[Polish space]] is a separable topological space homeomorphic to a complete metric space}}

{{term|pow}}
{{defn|defn=Abbreviation for "power (set)"}}

{{term|power}}
{{defn|defn="Power" is an archaic term for [[cardinality]]}}

{{term|power set}}
{{term|powerset|multi=y}}
{{defn|defn=The powerset or [[power set]] of a set is the set of all its subsets}}

{{term |1=pre-ordering}}
{{defn |1=A relation that is reflexive and transitive but not necessarily antisymmetric, allowing for the comparison of elements in a set.}}

{{term |1=primitive recursive set}}
{{defn |1=A set whose characteristic function is a primitive recursive function, indicating that membership in the set can be decided by a computable process.}}

{{term|projective}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[projective set]] is a set that can be obtained from an analytic set by repeatedly taking complements and projections}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Projective determinacy]] is an axiom asserting that projective sets are determined}}

{{term|proper}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[proper class]] is a class that is not a set}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[proper subset]] of a set ''X'' is a subset not equal to ''X''.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[proper forcing]] is a forcing notion that does not collapse any stationary set}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=The [[proper forcing axiom]] asserts that if ''P'' is proper and ''D<sub>α</sub>'' is a dense subset of ''P'' for each ''α''<''&omega;''<sub>1</sub>, then there is a filter <math>G \subseteq P</math> such that {{math|''D<sub>α</sub>'' ∩ ''G''}} is nonempty for all ''α''<''&omega;''<sub>1</sub>}}

{{term|PSP}}
{{defn|defn=[[Perfect subset property]]}}
{{glossary end}}

{{term |1=pure set}}
{{defn |1=A term for [[Hereditary set|hereditary sets]], which are sets that have only other sets as elements, that is, without any [[Urelement|urelements]].}}

{{term |1=pure set theory}}
{{defn |1=A set theory that deals only with pure sets, also known as [[Hereditary set|hereditary sets]]}}

==Q==
{{glossary}}

{{term|Q}}
{{defn|defn=The (ordered set of) rational numbers}}

{{term|QPD}}
{{defn|defn=Quasi-projective determinacy}}

{{term|quantifier}}
{{defn|defn=∀ or ∃}}

{{term|Quasi-projective determinacy}}
{{defn|defn=All sets of reals in ''L''(''R'') are determined}}

{{glossary end}}

==R==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝔯}}
{{defn|defn=The unsplitting number}}

{{term|R}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=''R''<sub>''α''</sub> is an alternative name for the level ''V''<sub>''α''</sub> of the [[von Neumann hierarchy]].}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The set of [[real number]]s, usually stylized as {{mathbb|R}}}}

{{term|Ramsey}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Frank P. Ramsey]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Ramsey cardinal]] is a large cardinal satisfying a certain partition condition}}

{{term|ran}}
{{defn|defn=The [[range of a function]]}}

{{term|rank}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The [[rank of a set]] is the smallest ordinal greater than the ranks of its elements}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A '''rank''' ''V''<sub>''α''</sub> is the collection of all sets of rank less than α, for an ordinal ''α''}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=[[rank-into-rank]] is a type of large cardinal (axiom)}}

{{term |1=recursive set}}
{{defn |1=A set for which membership can be decided by a recursive procedure or algorithm, also known as a decidable or [[computable set]].}}

{{term |1=recursively enumerable set}}
{{defn |1=A set for which there exists a Turing machine that will list all members of the set, possibly without halting if the set is infinite; also called "semi-decidable set" or "Turing recognizable set".}}

{{term|reflecting cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=A [[reflecting cardinal]] is a type of large cardinal whose strength lies between being weakly compact and Mahlo}}

{{term|reflection principle}}
{{defn|defn=A [[reflection principle]] states that there is a set similar in some way to the universe of all sets}}

{{term|regressive}}
{{defn|defn=A function ''f'' from a subset of an ordinal to the ordinal is called regressive if ''f''(''α'')<''α'' for all α in its domain}}

{{term|regular}}
{{defn|defn=A [[regular cardinal]] is one equal to its own cofinality; a [[Regular cardinal|regular ordinal]] is a [[limit ordinal]] that is equal to its own cofinality.}}

{{term|Reinhardt cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=A [[Reinhardt cardinal]] is a cardinal in a model ''V'' of ZF that is the critical point of an elementary embedding of ''V'' into itself}}

{{term|relation}}
{{defn|defn=A set or class whose elements are ordered pairs}}

{{term |1=[[relative complement]]}}
{{defn |1=The set of elements that are in one set but not in another, often denoted as <math>A \setminus B</math> for sets <math>A</math> and <math>B</math>.}}

{{term|Richard}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Jules Richard (mathematician)|Jules Richard]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Richard's paradox]] considers the real number whose ''n''th binary digit is the opposite of the ''n''th digit of the ''n''th definable real number}}

{{term |right-narrow}}
{{defn |1=A partially ordered set, (α,≤) in which for all b in α, {c:c∈α∧b≤c}
(the up-set of b) is a set.}}

{{term|RO}}
{{defn|defn=The [[regular open set]]s of a topological space or poset}}

{{term|Rowbottom}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Frederick Rowbottom]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Rowbottom cardinal]] is a large cardinal satisfying a certain partition condition}}

{{term|rud}}
{{defn|defn=The [[rudimentary closure]] of a set}}

{{term|rudimentary}}
{{defn|defn=A [[rudimentary function]] is a functions definable by certain elementary operations, used in the construction of the Jensen hierarchy}}

{{term|rudimentary set theory}}
{{defn|defn=See {{gli|basic set theory}}.}}

{{term|Russell}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Bertrand Russell]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Russell's paradox]] is that the set of all sets not containing themselves is contradictory so cannot exist}}

{{term|Russell set}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The set involved in [[Russell's paradox]]}}

{{glossary end}}

==S==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝔰}}
{{defn|defn=The splitting number}}

{{term|Satisfaction relation}}
{{defn|defn=See {{gli|⊧|⊨}}}}

{{term|SBH}}
{{defn|defn=Stationary basis hypothesis}}

{{term|SCH}}
{{defn|defn=[[Singular cardinal hypothesis]]}}

{{term|SCS}}
{{defn|defn=Semi-constructive system}}

{{term|Scott}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Dana Scott]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Scott's trick]] is a way of coding proper equivalence classes by sets by taking the elements of the class of smallest rank}}

{{term|second}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A set of second category is a set that is not of [[meager set|first category]]: in other words a set  that is not the union of a countable number of nowhere-dense sets.}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An ordinal of the second class is a countable infinite ordinal}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=An ordinal of the second kind is a limit ordinal or 0}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=[[Second order logic]] allows quantification over subsets as well as over elements of a model}}

{{term |1=semi-decidable set}}
{{defn |1=A set for which membership can be determined by a computational process that halts and accepts if the element is a member, but may not halt if the element is not a member.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Forster |first=Thomas |title=Logic, induction and sets |date=2003 |publisher=Cambridge Univ. Press |isbn=978-0-521-53361-4 |edition=1. publ |series=London Mathematical Society student texts |location=Cambridge}}</ref>}}

{{term|sentence}}
{{defn|defn=A formula with no unbound variables}}

{{term|separating set}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[separating set]] is a set containing a given set and disjoint from another given set}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[separating set]] is a set ''S'' of functions on a set such that for any two distinct points there is a function in ''S'' with different values on them.}}

{{term |1=separation axiom}}
{{defn |1=In set theory, sometimes refers to the [[Axiom schema of separation]];<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Bagaria |first1=Joan |title=Set theory: Centre de recerca matemàtica Barcelona, 2003-2004 |last2=Todorčević |first2=Stevo |date=2006 |publisher=Birkhäuser Verlag |others=Centre de recerca matemàtica |isbn=978-3-7643-7692-5 |series=Trends in mathematics |location=Basel Boston |pages=156}}</ref> not to be confused with the [[Separation axiom]] from [[topology]].}}

{{term|separative}}
{{defn|defn=A separative poset is one that can be densely embedded into the poset of nonzero elements of a Boolean algebra.}}

{{term|[[Set (mathematics)|set]]}}
{{defn|defn=A collection of distinct objects, considered as an object in its own right.}}

{{term|set-theoretic}}
{{defn|defn=An adjective referring to set theory. In combination with nouns, it creates the phrases "set-theoretic hierarchy" referring to [[cumulative hierarchy]], "set-theoretic paradox" referring to the [[paradoxes of set theory]], "set-theoretic successor" referring to a [[successor ordinal]] or [[successor cardinal]], and "set-theoretic realism" for [[Set-theoretic realism|the position in philosophy of mathematics]] which defends that sets, as conceived in set theory, exist independently of human thought and language, similar to [[mathematical Platonism]].}}

{{term |1=[[Singleton_(mathematics)|singleton]]}}
{{defn |1=A set containing exactly one element; its significance lies in its role in the definition of functions and in the formulation of mathematical and logical concepts.}}

{{term|SFIP}}
{{defn|defn=[[Strong finite intersection property]]}}

{{term|SH}}
{{defn|defn=[[Suslin's hypothesis]]}}

{{term|Shelah}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Saharon Shelah]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Shelah cardinal]] is a large cardinal that is the critical point of an elementary embedding satisfying certain conditions}}

{{term|shrewd cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=A [[shrewd cardinal]] is a type of large cardinal generalizing indecribable cardinals to transfinite levels}}

{{term|Sierpinski}}
{{term|Sierpiński|multi=y}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Wacław Sierpiński]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Sierpiński set]] is an uncountable subset of a real vector space whose intersection with every measure-zero set is countable}}

{{term|Silver}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Jack Silver]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Silver indiscernible]]s form a class {{mvar|I}} of ordinals such that {{math|''I'' &cap; ''L''<sub>''κ''</sub>}} is a set of indiscernibles for ''L''<sub>''κ''</sub> for every uncountable cardinal ''κ''}}

{{term|simply infinite set}}
{{defn|defn=A term sometimes used for [[Infinite set|infinite sets]], i.e., sets {{glossary link internal|equinumerous}} with {{glossary link internal|N|ℕ}}, to contrast them with [[Dedekind-infinite set|Dedekind-infinite sets]].<ref name="CookDictionary" /> In {{glossary link internal|ZF}}, it can be proved that all Dedekind-infinite sets are simply infinite, but the converse – that all simply infinite sets are Dedekind-infinite – can only be proved in {{glossary link internal|ZFC}}.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Lindström |first1=Sten |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=leeNa6ncWUYC |title=Logicism, Intuitionism, and Formalism: What Has Become of Them? |last2=Palmgren |first2=Erik |last3=Segerberg |first3=Krister |last4=Stoltenberg-Hansen |first4=Viggo |date=2008-11-25 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-1-4020-8926-8 |pages=5 |language=en}}</ref>}}

{{term|singular}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[singular cardinal]] is one that is not regular}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[singular cardinal hypothesis]] states that if ''&kappa;'' is any singular strong limit cardinal, then 2<sup>''&kappa;''</sup> = ''&kappa;''<sup>+</sup>.}}

{{term|SIS}}
{{defn|defn=Semi-intuitionistic system}}

{{term|Skolem}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Thoralf Skolem]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Skolem's paradox]] states that if ZFC is consistent there are countable models of it}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[Skolem function]] is a function whose value is something with a given property if anything with that property exists}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=The [[Skolem hull]] of a model is its closure under Skolem functions}}

{{term|small}}
{{defn|defn=A small large cardinal axiom is a large cardinal axiom consistent with the axiom ''V''=''L''}}

{{term|SOCA}}
{{defn|defn=[[Semi open coloring axiom]]}}

{{term|Solovay}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Robert M. Solovay]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Solovay model]] is a model of ZF in which every set of reals is measurable}}

{{term|special}}
{{defn|defn=A [[special Aronszajn tree]] is one with an order preserving map to the rationals}}

{{term|square}}
{{defn|defn=The [[square principle]] is a combinatorial principle holding in the constructible universe and some other inner models}}

{{term|standard model}}
{{defn|defn=A model of set theory where the relation &isin; is the same as the usual one.}}

{{term|stationary set}}
{{defn|defn=A [[stationary set]] is a subset of an ordinal intersecting every club set}}

{{term |1=[[Stratification (mathematics)|stratified]]}}
{{defn |1=A formula of set theory is stratified if and only if there is a function
<math>\sigma</math> which sends each variable appearing in <math>\phi</math> (considered as an item of syntax) to
a natural number (this works equally well if all integers are used) in such a way that
any atomic formula <math>x \in y</math> appearing in <math>\phi</math> satisfies <math>\sigma(x)+1 = \sigma(y)</math> and any [[atomic formula]] <math>x = y</math> appearing in <math>\phi</math> satisfies <math>\sigma(x) = \sigma(y)</math>.}}

{{term |1=[[strict ordering]]}}
{{defn |1=An ordering relation that is transitive and irreflexive, implying that no element is considered to be strictly before or after itself, and that the relation holds transitively.}}

{{term|strong}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The [[strong finite intersection property]] says that the intersection of any finite number of elements of a set is infinite}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[strong cardinal]] is a cardinal ''κ'' such that if ''λ'' is any ordinal, there is an elementary embedding with critical point ''κ'' from the universe into a transitive inner model containing all elements of ''V''<sub>''λ''</sub>}}

{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[strong limit cardinal]] is a (usually nonzero) cardinal that is larger than the powerset of any smaller cardinal}}

{{term|strongly}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[strongly inaccessible cardinal]] is a regular strong limit cardinal}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[strongly Mahlo cardinal]] is a strongly inaccessible cardinal such that the set of strongly inaccessible cardinals below it is stationary}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[strongly compact cardinal]] is a cardinal ''κ'' such that every ''κ''-complete filter can be extended to a ''κ'' complete ultrafilter}}
