{{term |1=[[subset]]}}
{{defn |1=A set whose members are all contained within another set, without necessarily being identical to it.}}

{{term|subtle cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=A [[subtle cardinal]] is a type of large cardinal closely related to ethereal cardinals}}

{{term|successor}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[successor cardinal]] is the smallest cardinal larger than some given cardinal}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[successor ordinal]] is the smallest ordinal larger than some given ordinal}}

{{term|such that}}
{{defn|defn=A condition used in the definition of a mathematical object}}

{{term|sunflower}}
{{defn|defn=A [[sunflower lemma|sunflower]], also called a delta system, is a collection of sets such that any two distinct sets have intersection ''X'' for some fixed set ''X''}}

{{term|Souslin}}
{{term|Suslin|multi=y}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Mikhail Yakovlevich Suslin]] (sometimes written Souslin)}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Suslin algebra]] is a Boolean algebra that is complete, atomless, countably distributive, and satisfies the countable chain condition}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[Suslin cardinal]] is a cardinal ''λ'' such that there exists a set ''P'' ⊂ 2<sup>''ω''</sup> such that ''P'' is ''λ''-Suslin but ''P'' is not ''λ''&prime;-Suslin for any ''λ''&prime; < ''λ''.}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=The [[Suslin hypothesis]] says that Suslin lines do not exist}}
{{defn|no=5|defn=A [[Suslin line]] is a complete dense unbounded totally ordered set satisfying the countable chain condition}}
{{defn|no=6|defn=The [[Suslin number]] is the supremum of the cardinalities of families of disjoint open non-empty sets}}
{{defn|no=7|defn=The [[Suslin operation]], usually denoted by ''A'', is an operation that constructs a set from a Suslin scheme}}
{{defn|no=8|defn=The [[Suslin problem]] asks whether Suslin lines exist}}
{{defn|no=9|defn=The [[Suslin property]] states that there is no uncountable family of pairwise disjoint non-empty open subsets}}
{{defn|no=10|A [[Suslin representation]] of a set of reals is a tree whose projection is that set of reals}}
{{defn|no=11|A [[Suslin scheme]] is a function with domain the finite sequences of positive integers}}
{{defn|no=12|A [[Suslin set]] is a set that is the image of a tree under a certain projection}}
{{defn|no=13|A [[Suslin space]] is the image of a Polish space under a continuous mapping}}
{{defn|no=14|A [[Suslin subset]] is a subset that is the image of a tree under a certain projection}}
{{defn|no=15|The [[analytic set|Suslin theorem]] about analytic sets states that a set that is analytic and coanalytic is Borel}}
{{defn|no=16|A [[Suslin tree]] is a tree of height ω<sub>1</sub> such that every branch and every antichain is at most countable.}}

{{term|supercompact}}
{{defn|defn=A [[supercompact cardinal]] is an uncountable cardinal ''&kappa;'' such that for every ''A'' such that Card(''A'') ≥ ''&kappa;'' there exists a [[normal measure]] over [''A'']<sup>''&kappa;''</sup>.}}

{{term|super transitive}}
{{term|supertransitive|multi=y}}
{{defn|defn=A [[supertransitive set]] is a transitive set that contains all subsets of all its elements}}

{{term |1=[[symmetric difference]]}}
{{defn |1=The set operation that yields the elements present in either of two sets but not in their intersection, effectively the elements unique to each set.}}

{{term|symmetric model}}
{{defn|defn=A [[symmetric model]] is a model of ZF (without the axiom of choice) constructed using a group action on a forcing poset}}

{{glossary end}}

==T==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝔱}}
{{defn|defn=The tower number}}

{{term|T}}
{{defn|defn=A [[tree (set theory)|tree]]}}

{{term|tall cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=A [[tall cardinal]] is a type of large cardinal that is the critical point of a certain sort of elementary embedding}}

{{term|Tarski}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Alfred Tarski]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Tarski's theorem about choice|Tarski's theorem]] states that the axiom of choice is equivalent to the existence of a bijection from ''X'' to ''X''×''X'' for all infinite sets ''X''}}

{{term|TC}}
{{defn|defn=The [[transitive closure]] of a set}}

{{term|total order}}
{{defn|defn=A [[total order]] is a relation that is transitive and antisymmetric such that any two elements are comparable}}

{{term|totally indescribable}}
{{defn|defn=A [[totally indescribable cardinal]] is a cardinal that is Π{{su|p=''m''|b=''n''}}-indescribable for all ''m'',''n''}}

{{term|transfinite}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=An infinite ordinal or cardinal number (see [[Transfinite number]])}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Transfinite induction]] is induction over ordinals}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=[[Transfinite recursion]] is recursion over ordinals}}

{{term|transitive}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[transitive relation]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[transitive closure]] of a set is the smallest transitive set containing it.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[transitive set]] or class is a set or class such that the membership relation is transitive on it.}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=A [[transitive model]] is a model of set theory that is transitive and has the usual membership relation}}

{{term|tree}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[tree (set theory)|tree]] is a partially ordered set (''T'', <) such that for each ''t'' ∈ ''T'', the set {''s'' ∈ ''T'' : ''s'' < ''t''} is well-ordered by the relation <}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[tree (descriptive set theory)|tree]] is a collection of finite sequences such that every prefix of a sequence in the collection also belongs to the collection.}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A cardinal κ has the [[tree property]] if there are no κ-Aronszajn trees}}

{{term |1=[[tuple]]}}
{{defn |1=An ordered list of elements, with a fixed number of components, used in mathematics and computer science to describe ordered collections of objects.}}

{{term |1=Turing recognizable set}}
{{defn |1=A set for which there exists a Turing machine that halts and accepts on any input in the set, but may either halt and reject or run indefinitely on inputs not in the set.}}

{{term|type class}}
{{defn|defn=A type class or class of types is the class of all [[order type]]s of a given cardinality, up to order-equivalence.}}

{{glossary end}}

==U==
{{glossary}}

{{term|𝔲}}
{{defn|defn=The ultrafilter number, the minimum possible cardinality of an ultrafilter base}}

{{term|Ulam}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Stanislaw Ulam]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=An [[Ulam matrix]] is a collection of subsets of a cardinal indexed by pairs of ordinals, that satisfies certain properties.}}

{{term|Ult}}
{{defn|defn=An [[ultrapower]] or [[ultraproduct]]}}

{{term|ultrafilter}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A maximal filter}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The ultrafilter number 𝔲 is the minimum possible cardinality of an ultrafilter base}}

{{term|ultrapower}}
{{defn|defn=An [[ultraproduct]] in which all factors are equal}}

{{term|ultraproduct}}
{{defn|defn=An [[ultraproduct]] is the quotient of a product of models by a certain equivalence relation}}

{{term|unfoldable cardinal}}
{{defn|defn=An [[unfoldable cardinal]] a cardinal κ such that for every ordinal λ and every transitive model ''M'' of cardinality ''κ'' of ZFC-minus-power set such that κ is in ''M'' and ''M'' contains all its sequences of length less than κ, there is a non-trivial elementary embedding ''j'' of ''M'' into a transitive model with the critical point of ''j'' being ''κ'' and {{math|{{itco|''j''}}(''κ'') ≥ ''λ''}}.}}

{{term|uniformity}}
{{defn|defn=The uniformity {{math|non(''I'')}} of {{mvar|I}} is the smallest cardinality of a subset of ''X'' not in the ideal {{mvar|I}} of subsets of ''X''}}

{{term|uniformization}}
{{defn|defn=[[uniformization (set theory)|Uniformization]] is a weak form of the axiom of choice, giving cross sections for special subsets of a product of two Polish spaces}}

{{term |1=[[Union (set theory)|union]]}}
{{defn |1=An operation in set theory that combines the elements of two or more sets to form a single set containing all the elements of the original sets, without duplication.}}

{{term|universal}}
{{term|universe|multi=y}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=The [[Universe (mathematics)|universal class]], or universe, is the class of all sets.}}
{{defn|defn=A [[universal quantifier]] is the quantifier "for all", usually written ∀}}

{{term |1=[[unordered pair]]}}
{{defn |1=A set of two elements where the order of the elements does not matter, distinguishing it from an ordered pair where the sequence of elements is significant. The [[axiom of pairing]] asserts that for any two objects, the unordered pair containing those objects exists.}}

{{term |1=[[Upper and lower bounds|upper bound]]}}
{{defn |1=In mathematics, an element that is greater than or equal to every element of a given set, used in the discussion of intervals, sequences, and functions.}}

{{term |1=upward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem}}
{{defn |1=A theorem in model theory stating that if a countable first-order theory has an infinite model, then it has models of all larger cardinalities, demonstrating the scalability of models in first-order logic. (See [[Löwenheim–Skolem theorem]])}}

{{term|urelement}}
{{defn|defn=An [[urelement]] is something that is not a set but allowed to be an element of a set}}

{{glossary end}}

==V==
{{glossary}}

{{term|''V''}}
{{defn|defn=''V'' is the universe of all sets, and the sets ''V''<sub>α</sub> form the [[Von Neumann hierarchy]]}}

{{term|1=''V''=''L''}}
{{defn|defn=The [[axiom of constructibility]]}}

{{term|Veblen}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Oswald Veblen]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=The [[Veblen hierarchy]] is a family of ordinal valued functions, special cases of which are called [[Veblen functions]].}}

{{term|[[Venn diagram]]}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A graphical representation of the logical relationships between sets, using overlapping circles to illustrate intersections, unions, and complements of sets.}}

{{term|von Neumann}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[John von Neumann]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[von Neumann ordinal]] is an ordinal encoded as the union of all smaller (von Neumann) ordinals}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=The [[von Neumann hierarchy]] is a cumulative hierarchy ''V''<sub>α</sub> with ''V''<sub>α+1</sub> the powerset of ''V''<sub>α</sub>.}}

{{term|Vopenka}}
{{term|Vopěnka|multi=y}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Petr Vopěnka]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Vopěnka's principle]] states that for every proper class of binary relations there is one elementarily embeddable into another}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[Vopěnka cardinal]] is an inaccessible cardinal κ such that and Vopěnka's principle holds for ''V''<sub>κ</sub>}}

{{glossary end}}

==W==
{{glossary}}

{{term|weakly}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=A [[weakly inaccessible cardinal]] is a regular weak limit cardinal}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[weakly compact cardinal]] is a cardinal κ (usually also assumed to be inaccessible) such that the infinitary language L<sub>κ,κ</sub> satisfies the weak compactness theorem}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=A [[weakly Mahlo cardinal]] is a cardinal  κ that is weakly inaccessible and such that the set of weakly inaccessible cardinals less than κ is stationary in κ}}

{{term|well-founded}}
{{defn|defn=A relation is called [[well-founded]] if every non-empty subset has a minimal element (otherwise it is "non-well-founded")}}

{{term|well-ordering}}
{{defn|defn=A [[well-ordering]] is a well founded relation, usually also assumed to be a total order}}

{{term|[[well-ordering principle]]}}
{{defn|defn=that the positive integers are well-ordered, i.e., every non-empty set of positive integers contains a least element}}

{{term|[[well-ordering theorem]]}}
{{defn|defn=that every set can be well-ordered}}

{{term|Wf}}
{{defn|defn=The class of well-founded sets, which is the same as the class of all sets if one assumes the axiom of foundation}}

{{term|Woodin}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Hugh Woodin]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=A [[Woodin cardinal]] is a type of large cardinal that is the critical point of a certain sort of elementary embedding, closely related to the axiom of projective determinacy}}

{{glossary end}}

==XYZ==
{{glossary}}

{{term|Z}}
{{defn|defn=[[Zermelo set theory]] without the axiom of choice}}

{{term|ZC}}
{{defn|defn=[[Zermelo set theory]] with the axiom of choice}}

{{term|Zermelo}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Ernst Zermelo]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Zermelo−Fraenkel set theory]] is the standard system of axioms for set theory}}
{{defn|no=3|defn=[[Zermelo set theory]] is similar to the usual Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory, but without the axioms of replacement and foundation}}
{{defn|no=4|defn=[[Zermelo's well-ordering theorem]] states that every set can be well ordered}}

{{term|ZF}}
{{defn|defn=[[Zermelo−Fraenkel set theory]] without the axiom of choice}}

{{term|ZFA}}
{{defn|defn=[[Zermelo−Fraenkel set theory]] with atoms}}

{{term|ZFC}}
{{defn|defn=[[Zermelo−Fraenkel set theory]] with the axiom of choice}}

{{term |1=[[zero function]]}}
{{defn |1=A mathematical function that always returns the value zero, regardless of the input, often used in discussions of functions, calculus, and algebra.}}

{{term|ZF-P}}
{{defn|defn=[[Zermelo−Fraenkel set theory]] without the axiom of choice or the powerset axiom}}

{{term|Zorn}}
{{defn|no=1|defn=[[Max August Zorn|Max Zorn]]}}
{{defn|no=2|defn=[[Zorn's lemma]] states that if every chain of a non-empty poset has an upper bound then the poset has a maximal element}}

{{glossary end}}
